message.content:
**Welch Allyn** ophthalmology tools are mainly **diagnostic eye-exam instruments** such as **ophthalmoscopes**, **otoscopes**, **retinoscopes**, and related **ophthalmic sets**. The latest product lines highlighted in the results include the **PanOptic Plus Ophthalmoscope** and the **MacroView Plus Otoscope**, which are designed for wider, brighter views and can be paired with digital capture accessories.[2][3][4]

Common Welch Allyn ophthalmology tools in the results include:

- **PanOptic Plus Ophthalmoscope** — a wide-view ophthalmoscope intended to improve optic disc viewing during eye exams, with **Quick Eye alignment** support.[2][3][4]
- **Traditional ophthalmoscopes** — handheld instruments used to examine the **retina**; Welch Allyn offers several versions, including pocket and 3.5 V models.[1][4]
- **MacroView Plus Otoscope** — an ear-exam tool that can also support image capture when used with the **iExaminer SmartBracket** and a smart device.[2][4]
- **Ophthalmic sets** — bundled diagnostic kits that combine an ophthalmoscope, power handle, and sometimes other instruments.[3][5]
- **Retinoscopes** — listed as part of the Welch Allyn catalogue of eye-exam tools.[1][6]
- **Transilluminators and vision screeners** — also sold under Welch Allyn in ophthalmic/diagnostic instrument catalogs.[6]

If you want, I can also give you:
- a **plain-English explanation** of what each tool does,
- a **buying guide** for Welch Allyn eye tools,
- or a **comparison** of **PanOptic Plus vs standard ophthalmoscopes**.
